![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261478/assets/f0d6ec515c60c3bdda815f57005ece7d4de7de0a8251058542a0627da4366083.png)

Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}dA,$
where $D$ is the finite region below the line $y=3$ enclosed by the lines $y=\frac{x}{3}$ and $x=6.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $D$ is a type I region.

- We already know the intersection of the line $y=\frac{x}{3}$ with the line $y=3.$
So, the $x$-limits are 
$6\le x\le 9.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14261478/assets/cd1948c65b6bec22f43b07fce2bcc54840f026457dda49115b4a0f8adf37a381.png)

As a result, the integral is defined over the following type I region: 

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,6\le x\le 9,\,\frac{x}{3}\le y\le 3\}
$$

So, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}dA={\int }_{6}^{9}{\int }_{x/3}^{3}dy\,dx
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{6}^{9}{\int }_{x/3}^{3}dy\,dx & ={\int }_{6}^{9}[{\int }_{x/3}^{3}dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{6}^{9}[y]_{x/3}^{3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{6}^{9}(3-\frac{x}{3})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{6}^{9}(3-\frac{x}{3})\,dx & ={[3x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{6}]}_{6}^{9} \\  & =27-\frac{81}{6}-(18-\frac{36}{6}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
